name: skylighting
description: Haskell port of KDE syntax definitions; powers Pandoc's highlighting across HTML, LaTeX, docx, ANSI

host-language.comment: Pure Haskell library, published on Hackage.

form-factor.comment: Library (skylighting-core plus the skylighting package with bundled syntaxes and formatters). The `skylighting` CLI is built when the cabal `executable` flag is set. It outputs ansi, html, latex, context, typst and native.

license.comment: Engine (skylighting-core) is BSD-3-Clause. The `skylighting` package, which bundles the generated syntax modules, is GPL-2.0-only because some KDE XML definitions it is built from are GPL. Individual XML files carry their own licences (e.g. html.xml is LGPL).

package.comment: Split into skylighting-core, skylighting-format-{ansi,blaze-html,context,latex,typst}, and the umbrella skylighting package.

documentation.comment: No dedicated docs site. Documentation is the README plus Haddock API reference on Hackage.

first-release.comment: Changelog lists 0.1.0.0 (initial release) dated 2016-12-23. It succeeded highlighting-kate.

engine-model.comment: Parses KDE XML syntax definitions into Haskell data structures that a generic `tokenize` function interprets, so IncludeRules work properly.

regex-engine.comment: Since 0.9 it uses a pure-Haskell regex implementation (Regex.KDE, exposed via Skylighting.Regex) instead of pcre, to drop the C dependency. The changelog notes this was slower than pcre.

embedded-languages.comment: Uses KDE IncludeRules: html.xml includes `##CSS` for <style> and `Normal##JavaScript` for <script>. The README says IncludeRules are handled properly by the interpreter.

language-auto-detection.comment: Lookup works only by name, short name, extension or filename. The CLI has no content-based detection.

filename-extension-mapping.comment: `syntaxesByExtension`, `syntaxesByFilename` and `lookupSyntax` use the extension globs in the KDE definitions (sExtensions).

resumable-line-state.comment: The only entry point is `tokenize :: TokenizerConfig -> Syntax -> Text -> Either String [SourceLine]`. It works on a whole buffer and exposes no per-line state.

incremental-reparsing.comment: No edit/reparse API; every call tokenizes the full input.

semantic-distinctions.comment: Regex/context state machine (KDE syntax) with a fixed set of 31 lexical token types. There is no syntax tree.

bundled-languages.comment: 195 .xml syntax definitions in skylighting-core/xml as of 0.15.0.1 (counted 2026-11-18). This includes a few include-only helper syntaxes (e.g. alert, comments, doxygen, javadoc, modelines, spdx-comments, todo), so the number of standalone languages is slightly lower.

grammar-format.comment: KDE KSyntaxHighlighting XML syntax definitions. Some are lightly patched (.xml.patch files in the repo).

grammar-ecosystem-compatibility.comment: Consumes KDE syntax XML directly, both at build time (bundled) and at runtime. Regex features unsupported by the pure-Haskell engine may limit some definitions.

runtime-grammar-loading.comment: `loadSyntaxFromFile` and `loadSyntaxesFromDir` load KDE XML at runtime. The CLI has `-d/--definition` and Pandoc has `--syntax-definition`.

lazy-grammar-loading.comment: Bundled syntaxes are compiled into the auto-generated `defaultSyntaxMap`. There is no documented on-demand loading (Haskell laziness aside).

grammar-accuracy.comment: Spot check 2026-11-18: python.xml (v33) handles match/case and f-strings. typescript.xml (v18) lacks `satisfies`, `override`, `accessor` and `using` keywords. The grammars are periodically synced copies of KDE's hand-maintained definitions (same versions as KSyntaxHighlighting). Rated 3 for known gaps on modern syntax.

bundled-themes.comment: As of 0.15.0.1: kate, breezeDark, pygments, espresso, tango, haddock, monochrome and zenburn. The CLI `-S` option lists only 7 (no zenburn).

theme-format.comment: Built-in styles are Haskell `Style` values. `parseTheme` and the FromJSON instance read KDE JSON .theme files.

token-classification.comment: Closed `TokenType` enum of 31 constructors (KeywordTok, FunctionTok, StringTok, ... NormalTok), mirroring KDE default styles. HTML class names are short forms like `kw`.

css-class-output.comment: HTML formatter emits spans with short classes (e.g. KeywordTok -> `kw`). `styleToCss` generates the stylesheet for a Style.

multi-theme-output.comment: Class-based HTML with one `styleToCss` stylesheet per Style. There is no single-render light/dark mechanism. Quarto builds light/dark support on top by swapping theme CSS.

public-token-api.comment: `tokenize` returns `[SourceLine]`, where SourceLine = [Token] and Token = (TokenType, Text). This is the documented input to all formatters.

ir-kinds.comment: A list of lines of (TokenType, Text) pairs.

serializable-ir.comment: TokenType has ToJSON/FromJSON and Binary instances (and Style has a documented KDE-theme JSON mapping), so aeson can encode token lists generically. However, there is no documented serialization format for token streams, and the CLI `native` output is a Haskell `ppShow` debug dump. Strict reading of the guideline gives false.

theme-resolved-tokens.comment: Tokens carry only a TokenType. Colours come from looking up `tokenStyles` in a Style map. No API emits tokens with resolved styles.

source-offsets-in-ir.comment: Token = (TokenType, Text) with no offsets. Line position is implicit only in the list index.

custom-formatter-api.comment: No formal typeclass. A formatter is a function `FormatOptions -> [SourceLine] -> output`. The official formatters live in separate skylighting-format-* packages built on the public types, and Pandoc writes its own (e.g. docx) the same way.

line-transforms-decorations.comment: FormatOptions only cover line numbers, start number, line anchors, title attributes, classes, ID prefix and ANSI colour level. There is no range/line annotation mechanism.

output-formats.comment: First-party formatters: HTML (blaze-html, class-based), ANSI (16/256/truecolor via ansiColorLevel), LaTeX, ConTeXt and Typst (no tags for the last two). Pandoc's docx/ms highlighting is implemented in Pandoc, not skylighting.

line-numbers.comment: `numberLines` and `startNumber` in FormatOptions. CLI flags are `-n` and `-N`.

streaming-output.comment: No documented incremental API. `tokenize` takes the complete Text, and the CLI reads the whole input before tokenizing.

terminal-ready.comment: Skylighting.Format.ANSI. The CLI defaults to ANSI with auto colour-level detection from COLORTERM/TERM.

native-dependencies.comment: Pure Haskell since 0.9 replaced pcre with its own regex engine. No C libraries in the dependency list.

runs-in-browser.comment: No official browser build of skylighting itself. It does run in the browser indirectly as part of Pandoc's official WASM build (pandoc 3.9+, pandoc.org/app).

wasm-build.comment: Skylighting ships no WASM artifact. Being pure Haskell, it compiles with GHC's wasm32 backend as part of pandoc.wasm (pandoc 3.9+).

synchronous-api.comment: `tokenize` is a pure function. Only runtime loading of XML definitions is in IO.

bindings-ports.comment: No official bindings found. It is mostly consumed in other ecosystems through the Pandoc CLI or Quarto.

core-package-size.comment: Compiled Haskell library (bundled syntaxes are generated into Haskell modules). Not comparable with JS bundle or wheel/crate sizes.

throughput-tier.comment: Only internal benchmarks exist (vs highlighting-kate and across its own releases). The 0.9 changelog notes a slowdown from the pure-Haskell regex. No cross-engine benchmark was found.

initialization-cost.comment: Unmeasured; no published timing for first highlight.

monthly-downloads.comment: Hackage downloads in the last 30 days, checked 2026-11-18 (skylighting-core: 571). Hackage counts miss Stackage/Nix/distro and Pandoc binary installs, so they heavily understate real use.

maintenance-status.comment: Release 0.15.0.1 on 2026-11-10 and last push the same day. There are frequent releases (~110 versions) and syntax updates tracking KDE.

documentation-quality.comment: Rated 2. The README covers architecture, packages and the CLI. The Haddock reference is terse (e.g. `tokenize` has no prose description), with no usage examples, guides, or syntax/theme catalog beyond the Styles module.

notable-users.comment: pandoc.cabal depends on skylighting/skylighting-core >= 0.15.0.1. Quarto docs say highlighting is implemented using skylighting. Hakyll uses it transitively through its pandoc dependency.

bus-factor.comment: John MacFarlane (jgm) has 924 commits; the next contributor has 28.
